paragraphs.en: In Cloudpine Valley, winter did not end on the same day every year. Tavi, a young red panda, woke before the sun. A small bug moved across the window. She opened it and listened, but there were no bird calls. Her camera hung beside the door. She took a picture of the white hills, yet a picture could not show the silence. That was the first fact she wrote in her book. A friendly woman at the next house offered warm juice. Tavi thanked her but kept looking toward the trees. She had always loved the first sound of spring. Today the valley seemed to be holding its breath.
paragraphs.zh: 雲松谷的冬天並不是每年都在同一天結束。年輕的小熊貓塔薇在日出前醒來。一隻小蟲爬過窗戶。她打開窗戶聽，卻聽不見鳥叫聲。相機掛在門邊，她拍下白色山丘，但照片無法呈現這片寂靜。這是她寫進筆記本的第一個事實。隔壁一位友善的女士送來溫熱果汁。塔薇道謝，仍望向樹林。她一直喜歡春天的第一個聲音。今天整座山谷卻像屏住了呼吸。

paragraphs.en: Her friend Ivo, a mountain goat, came from the north path. He had a red hat and a pet mouse in a warm little box. “I will not lie to you,” he said kindly. “I heard no birds on the north path either. But there may be birds on the other side of the hill.” Tavi stood in the middle of the yard and tried to notice every little noise. She heard a step, a falling leaf, and Ivo's mouse eating. No song came from the woods. They did not say that spring was gone. They said only that they had not heard it yet. It was an important difference, and Tavi marked it in her book.
paragraphs.zh: 她的朋友、山羊伊沃從北邊小路走來。他戴著紅帽子，還帶著一隻住在溫暖小盒裡的寵物老鼠。「我不會騙妳，」他溫和地說，「北邊小路上我也沒聽到鳥鳴。不過山丘另一邊可能還有鳥。」塔薇站在院子中央，努力注意每一個小聲音。她聽到腳步、落葉，以及伊沃的老鼠吃東西的聲音，卻沒有樹林裡的歌聲。他們沒有說春天消失了，只說目前還沒有聽見。這兩種說法並不相同，塔薇把差別寫進筆記本。

paragraphs.en: A picnic was planned for the first warm day. Other families wanted to walk up the high hill then, but the snow there was still deep. Tavi could not reach the old lookout safely. She would not use a dangerous road just to get an answer quickly. Instead, she drew a simple map of the lower valley. This was a place where young and old neighbors could walk together. A bright star was still high in the pale morning sky. Ivo pointed to it, then pointed to the low path. “One thing is far away,” he said. “The other is here under our feet. We can start here.”
paragraphs.zh: 大家原本計畫在第一個溫暖的日子野餐。其他家庭想走上高丘，但那裡的雪仍然很深。塔薇無法安全抵達舊瞭望台。她不願為了快速找到答案就使用危險的路。於是她畫了一張山谷低地的簡單地圖。年輕與年長的鄰居都能一起走這段路。清晨淡淡的天空仍掛著一顆明亮星星。伊沃先指星星，再指低處小路。「有個東西很遠，」他說，「另一個就在腳下。我們可以從這裡開始。」

paragraphs.en: Tavi wanted the future spring walk to be safe for everyone. She asked Ivo to help, but she also wanted someone who knew the ground under the snow. They went to see Nell, a marmot who lived near the warm rocks. Nell knew where small streams ran and where ice stayed thin. She agreed to join only if they turned back when a path felt wrong. “We are looking for sounds, not prizes,” she said. Tavi liked that rule. They made one more rule: never take an animal from its home simply to hear it make a sound.
paragraphs.zh: 塔薇希望未來的春季散步對每個人都安全。她請伊沃幫忙，也想找一位懂得雪下土地情況的朋友。他們去見住在溫暖岩石旁的土撥鼠奈兒。奈兒知道小溪流向，也知道哪些地方的冰很薄。她答應加入，但條件是道路一旦不對勁就立刻折返。「我們找的是聲音，不是獎品，」她說。塔薇喜歡這個原則。他們還訂下另一條規則：絕不為了聽叫聲，就把動物帶離自己的家。

paragraphs.en: By noon, the three friends had a plan, a pencil, and three warm coats. They would listen near the homes first, move farther only with care, and share what they learned with the valley. Nobody promised to bring spring back. Spring was not a thing that could be carried in a bag. Still, they could learn why the morning felt so different. Tavi closed her book and smiled at her friends. She no longer needed to wait alone beside her window. The search had begun, and her first real job was simple: listen before deciding what the silence meant.
paragraphs.zh: 中午前，三位朋友已備好計畫、鉛筆與三件暖外套。他們會先在住家附近聆聽，確認安全後才走遠，並把發現告訴山谷居民。沒有人承諾把春天帶回來，因為春天不是能裝進袋子的東西。不過，他們可以了解今天的早晨為何如此不同。塔薇合起筆記本，對朋友笑了。她再也不必獨自站在窗邊等待。尋找已經開始，而她的第一項工作很簡單：先聽，再判斷沉默的意思。

paragraphs.en: That afternoon, Tavi went back to the same window and compared what she heard at dawn with what she heard now. A cart passed outside. A family laughed on the road. The quiet in the woods was still there, but the whole valley had never been silent. She made two small columns in her book: sounds made by neighbors and sounds made by the land. It was not a perfect way to sort the world, yet it helped her ask a better question. Ivo returned to check that she had eaten. Nell brought a spare pencil and reminded her to rest. Tavi was grateful. She could look for the spring sounds without turning every hour into work. Before going to bed, she wrote, “We may hear something tomorrow, or we may hear nothing new. Both days can teach us.” The line made her feel ready for morning.
paragraphs.zh: 當天下午，塔薇回到同一扇窗邊，比較黎明與此刻聽見的聲音。外面有推車經過，路上有家庭在笑。樹林仍安靜，但整座山谷從未完全無聲。她在本子分成兩欄：鄰居製造的聲音，以及土地傳來的聲音。這不是完美的分類方法，卻幫她提出更好的問題。伊沃回來確認她吃過飯，奈兒帶來備用鉛筆，也提醒她休息。塔薇很感激。她可以尋找春聲，不必讓每個小時都變成工作。睡前，她寫下：「明天也許聽見新聲音，也許什麼都沒有。兩種日子都能教我們一些事。」這句話讓她準備好迎接早晨。

questions.question: What was missing from the woods that morning?
questions.explanation: 第一、二段明確寫出沒有鳥叫聲；塔薇仍看到小蟲，也聽到其他聲響，因此並非所有生命都消失。

questions.question: Why did the friends choose a low path?
options: The high hill was still snowy and unsafe.
They wanted to find a lost letter.
questions.explanation: 高處山丘仍有深雪，低地路線較安全。

title: A Meeting by the Warm Stones

paragraphs.en: The friends met at Nell's apartment, a small home cut into a warm hillside. Anybody could come to the meeting, so a few neighbors sat on flat stones by the door. Nell began by asking them not to guess about the weather. An old church stood across the valley, but its road was too icy today. “We can stay here,” she said. “The ground is clear, and we can hear each other.” A visiting reporter had come to learn why there were so few birds. Tavi asked him to write only what they knew. It was a serious question, not a game to win.
paragraphs.zh: 朋友們在奈兒的公寓開會，那是山坡裡一間溫暖的小屋。任何人都能參加，幾位鄰居便坐在門邊平石上。奈兒先請大家不要憑空猜測天氣。山谷對面有座舊教堂，但通往那裡的路今天太滑。「我們留在這裡就好，」她說，「地面安全，也聽得見彼此。」一位來訪的記者想知道為何鳥如此少。塔薇請他只寫已知事實。這是嚴肅的問題，不是要爭輸贏的遊戲。

paragraphs.en: An old deer from another country spoke next. She told them about a winter when birds arrived late. She had almost forgotten the date, but she still remembered the first small call from the hill. Ivo picked up a pen and drew three places on a piece of paper: the lower pond, the pine grove, and the meadow. Nell said they should visit the pond first. Water could change before trees did. They would take lunch, not stay away past dark, and call home if the trip changed. A small telephone lay on the shelf beside Nell's sofa.
paragraphs.zh: 接著，一隻來自另一個國家的老鹿說起往事。她記得有一年鳥兒到得很晚；日期幾乎忘了，但山上第一聲細小鳥叫仍記得清楚。伊沃拿起筆，在一張紙上畫出三處：低地池塘、松林及草地。奈兒建議先去池塘，因為水的變化可能早於樹木。他們會帶午餐、天黑前回來，行程變動時便打電話回家。奈兒的沙發旁架子上放著一部電話。

paragraphs.en: The reporter asked whether the town would pay for a guide. Nell explained that they needed no money for the short walk, but a guide might be needed for the high snow later. She showed a third path on the map, then crossed it out. It passed under loose rocks. “If we are late, we turn back,” she said. “If the ice is not safe, we turn back. If anyone feels tired, we stop.” Tavi listened to every word. She had wanted an answer at once, but she now saw that a good answer could take time.
paragraphs.zh: 記者問鎮上會不會付錢請嚮導。奈兒解釋，這段短路不需要花錢，但以後若要去高處雪地，可能得有嚮導。她指著地圖上的第三條路，隨即把它劃掉，因為那條路在鬆動岩石下方。「如果太晚，就折返；冰面不安全，就折返；有人累了，就停下。」塔薇仔細聽。她本來想立刻得到答案，如今知道好答案有時需要時間。

paragraphs.en: A little mole arrived with a bowl of hot soup. He could not see the far hill well, but he knew the sound of water under stones. He offered to describe it when they returned. Nell smiled because that was just the kind of help they needed. Here was a neighbor who could add knowledge without taking a dangerous walk. The visitors made room for him beside the fire. They did not ask him to prove anything on the spot. His experience was useful, and his comfort mattered as much as theirs.
paragraphs.zh: 一隻小鼴鼠端著熱湯來到。他看不清遠處山丘，卻熟悉石頭底下的水聲，願意等他們回來後協助辨認。奈兒微笑，因為這正是他們需要的幫助。眼前這位鄰居不用冒險走遠路，也能提供知識。大家在火旁讓出位子，沒有要求他當場證明什麼。他的經驗很有用，而他的舒適與其他人的舒適一樣重要。

paragraphs.en: At the end of the meeting, Tavi read the plan back to the group. She did not leave out the warnings. One neighbor said the notes sounded too careful for a search for spring. Nell answered that being careful was the reason they could go at all. The reporter put down his notebook and thanked them. Tomorrow he would walk only as far as the first safe turn. Tavi watched the neighbors go home. They had no new bird call yet, but now the valley had a clear way to look for one.
paragraphs.zh: 會議結束前，塔薇把計畫念給大家聽，連警告也沒有省略。有位鄰居說，尋找春天何必這麼小心。奈兒回答，正因為小心，他們才有機會出發。記者放下筆記本向大家道謝，明天他只會走到第一個安全的轉彎處。塔薇看著鄰居回家。雖然他們仍沒聽見新的鳥鳴，但山谷終於有了一個清楚的尋找方法。

paragraphs.en: After the visitors went away, Nell asked Tavi to help clean the meeting place. They folded the chairs, put away the cups, and checked the door. Tavi almost left the safety notes on the table. “Do not forget them,” Nell said. “Those notes belong to the whole plan.” Tavi put the paper in her bag and read the first line aloud once more. It said that a path must be checked on the day of a walk, not only the day before. She thought of the families who might read their report. They would need clear words and real dates, not a brave-sounding story. Ivo waited outside and kept the path free for the older deer. When all three friends reached home, they sent a short note to the others. Tomorrow's walk would begin only after the morning check. Everyone now knew what to expect.
paragraphs.zh: 訪客離開後，奈兒請塔薇一起打掃會議場所。他們收好椅子和杯子，也檢查了門。塔薇差點把安全筆記留在桌上。「別忘了它，」奈兒說，「那是整個計畫的一部分。」塔薇把紙收進袋子，又念了一遍第一行：步道應在出發當天檢查，而不只是前一天。她想起可能閱讀報告的家庭。大家需要清楚的字句與真實日期，不是聽起來勇敢的故事。伊沃在外頭等，並為老鹿留下通道。三位朋友都回家後，他們寄出一份簡短通知。明天早晨完成檢查後才會出發。現在每個人都知道該期待什麼。

questions.question: Where was the first group meeting?
questions.explanation: 大家在奈兒山坡裡的小家開會。

questions.question: What did they do with the path under loose rocks?
questions.explanation: 奈兒把鬆動岩石下方的路從地圖上劃掉。

paragraphs.en: All the paths near the lower pond looked white, but Nell knew the area well. She told Tavi to begin at a tree with three low branches. Two young goats were playing basketball near their home. Their ball made a loud sound against a wall. Tavi laughed, then stopped to define the sound they wanted to hear: not every noise was a sign of spring. Ivo asked the goats to keep playing; this search was not a reason to stop other people from having fun. The friends walked to the pond on a clear path that did not cross the ice.
paragraphs.zh: 低地池塘附近所有道路看來都是白的，但奈兒很熟悉這一帶。她要塔薇從一棵長著三根低樹枝的樹開始走。兩隻年輕山羊正在家旁打籃球，球撞牆時發出很大的聲音。塔薇笑了，隨後停下來界定他們要找的聲音：不是每個聲響都代表春天。伊沃請小山羊繼續玩，尋聲不是阻止別人玩樂的理由。三人沿著安全小路走向池塘，沒有踏上冰面。

paragraphs.en: Nell carried a modern little lamp, though it was still day. She also brought an eraser because maps can be wrong. Tavi had only a few marks on her page. They listened beside an orange plant pot left near the shore by a gardener. Under the ice came a soft tick, then another. Nell said it could be moving water, or it could be ice moving with the sun. “We need less guessing and more listening,” she said. Ivo took a note but left a little space beside it. One sound alone was not enough to tell the whole story.
paragraphs.zh: 奈兒帶了一盞新式小燈，雖然仍是白天。她也帶著橡皮擦，因為地圖可能畫錯。塔薇的筆記頁上只有少數記號。三人在岸邊園丁留下的橘色花盆旁聽著。冰下面傳來細小的喀聲，接著又一聲。奈兒說，那可能是流動的水，也可能是冰在陽光下移動。「少猜一些，多聽一些，」她說。伊沃做了紀錄，卻在旁邊留一點空白。單一聲音還不足以說明整件事。

paragraphs.en: A ranger came by at a quarter past one. He could not leave the main path because he had work to do. He asked them to send an email with their notes instead of making a long trip to his office. “You may also mail a paper copy,” he said, “but the road has heavy traffic in the afternoon.” Tavi wrote both choices down. She did not need to use the road today. She could go home before night and share the notes from there. The ranger added that some winter sounds grew louder when the day became warm.
paragraphs.zh: 一點十五分時，一位巡守員走來。他還有工作，不能離開主要道路，便請三人用電子郵件寄送紀錄，不必遠行到辦公室。「也可以郵寄紙本，」他說，「但下午道路交通很忙。」塔薇把兩種方法都記下來。今天不用走那條路，她可以天黑前回家，再分享筆記。巡守員還說，有些冬天的聲音會在天氣變暖時更加清楚。

paragraphs.en: At three p.m., the friends heard a thin line of water moving under the snow beside the bank. They could not see it, so Nell drew a small question mark rather than a picture of a stream. Tavi was happy with that. She had learned that good field notes tell what happened, not what the writer wished to happen. Ivo found a dry stick and set it beside the path to mark a safe place to stand. No one touched the ice. They stayed for five more minutes, then walked back before the wind grew cold.
paragraphs.zh: 下午三點，他們聽見岸邊積雪下似乎有一條細流在移動。因為看不到，奈兒畫了一個小問號，而不是直接畫溪流。塔薇很滿意。她學到好的野外紀錄應該寫發生的事，而不是作者希望發生的事。伊沃找到一根乾樹枝，放在小路邊標出安全站立的位置。沒有人碰冰面。五分鐘後，大家在風變冷前走回家。

paragraphs.en: At home, Tavi put the words “first possible water sound” on the page. The word possible mattered. Tomorrow the sun might be brighter, or the pond might sound different. She would compare both days before giving the sound a name. Nell warmed her paws, and Ivo hung the coats near the door. They were tired but not disappointed. The first trip had given them something better than a fast answer: a way to ask the same question again and check it with care.
paragraphs.zh: 回家後，塔薇在紙上寫下「第一個可能的水聲」。「可能」這兩個字很重要。明天陽光也許更亮，池塘也可能發出不同聲音。她決定比較兩天的結果，再為聲音命名。奈兒暖著爪子，伊沃把外套掛在門旁。他們累了，卻不失望。第一次出門帶來的不是快速答案，而是一套能再次提問並仔細查證的方法。

paragraphs.en: That evening, Tavi read her notes to her friends. The line about the small sound under the ice had a question mark beside it. “We will check it again when the weather is safe,” she said. “We will not change the word possible into certain just because we want a good story.” Nell agreed and drew a second box for the next visit. Ivo said he had learned to enjoy questions that were not finished yet. When a question stayed open, they had a reason to return with care and compare days. Tavi looked at the pale picture on her camera. It showed the pond, the dry path, and the far trees. It did not show the soft sound. That was why she needed words as well as pictures. She closed the book before dinner, knowing that a good search could leave room for tomorrow.
paragraphs.zh: 傍晚，塔薇把紀錄念給朋友聽。冰下細聲那行旁邊留著問號。「天氣安全時，我們會再檢查，」她說，「不能只因想說好故事，就把『可能』改成『確定』。」奈兒同意，在紙上畫了第二次拜訪的空格。伊沃說他開始喜歡尚未完成的問題。問題保持開放，就有理由日後小心回來比較。塔薇看著相機裡淡淡的照片，上面有池塘、乾路和遠樹，卻沒有聲音。因此她除了照片，也需要文字。晚飯前她合起本子，知道好的探索應為明天留下空間。

questions.question: What sound did the friends hear near the pond?
options: A small sound under the ice.
questions.explanation: 他們在池塘冰層下聽見微弱聲響。

questions.question: Why did Nell draw a question mark?
options: She was not sure what made the sound.
questions.explanation: 看不見來源，因此奈兒不把推測寫成確定事實。

paragraphs.en: The next day, the three friends met by an outdoor bath fed by warm mountain water. A large block of snow lay on the path beyond it. Both Nell and Ivo knew they had a choice: turn around or cross the open field to the east. The field looked green where the wind had moved the snow, but that did not make it safe. Tavi shook her head when a young animal wanted to run across. “We must not pass a place we have not checked,” she said. The child carried a cute wooden duck and went back to the bath with his family.
paragraphs.zh: 隔天，三人在一座有山泉暖水的露天浴池旁集合。前面的路被大雪塊擋住。奈兒和伊沃都知道有兩個選擇：折返，或穿過東邊的空地。風吹走部分積雪後，空地露出綠色，但那不代表安全。一隻小動物想跑過去時，塔薇搖頭說：「沒有檢查的地方，我們不能通過。」那孩子拿著可愛的木鴨，與家人一起回到浴池旁。

paragraphs.en: Nell took a bowl and a closed flask from her bag. She poured warm water into the bowl so Tavi could warm her cold hands. She did not pour it on the ground; warm water could make new ice later. Ivo made a medium-size mark in the snow at the safe stopping place. A gentle knock came from a wooden door nearby. Mrs. Alder, an old mountain sheep, asked what they were looking for. Tavi gave an honest answer. “We look for signs of spring, but we have not found a safe road ahead.” Mrs. Alder nodded. She knew the hill behind her house and offered to show them another way on a map.
paragraphs.zh: 奈兒從袋子取出碗和蓋緊的保溫瓶，把溫水倒進碗裡，讓塔薇暖一暖凍冷的雙手。她沒有把水倒在地上，因為熱水晚些可能重新結冰。伊沃在安全停步處的雪上留下中等大小的記號。附近木門傳來輕敲聲。年長的綿羊奧德太太問他們在找什麼。塔薇誠實回答：「我們在找春天的跡象，可是前面的路還不安全。」奧德太太點頭。她熟悉屋後山坡，願意在地圖上指出另一條路。

paragraphs.en: The family invited them to look at a drawing of the hill, not to walk it today. From the window, the friends could see a thin line where the snow had fallen away. The road below it was quiet, with no moving stones. But the surprise was on the drawing itself. Mrs. Alder had marked an old water course that ran beneath the field. That could explain why the surface looked green. The place was not open land at all. Warm water might be moving under it. Their careful choice had kept them away from weak ground.
paragraphs.zh: 這家人請他們先看看山坡圖，而不是今天就去走。從窗邊可以看到一條積雪退去的細線，下面的道路十分安靜，沒有石頭滾動。但驚喜在圖紙上：奧德太太標出空地下方一條舊水道。這可能解釋地表為何呈綠色。那裡並非普通空地，底下可能有暖水流動。三人因謹慎選擇，避開了可能鬆軟的地面。

paragraphs.en: Ivo made tea, and Nell wrote down the new information. Tavi looked carefully at Mrs. Alder's map. She did not add a new sound to the list because they had not heard one. They did add a place to avoid until the ground was checked by someone who knew it. The older sheep was pleased that the children listened. “A map is a promise to tell the truth,” she said. “It is not a reason to walk somewhere simply because a line looks short.” Tavi copied that thought into her book.
paragraphs.zh: 伊沃泡了茶，奈兒寫下新資料。塔薇仔細看奧德太太的地圖。因為沒有親耳聽到新的聲音，她沒有把什麼加進聲音清單。但他們標註了一處暫時不可進入的地方，直到熟悉地形的人完成檢查。老綿羊很高興年輕人願意聽。「地圖是說實話的承諾，」她說，「不是因為線畫得短就非走不可的理由。」塔薇把這句話抄進本子。

paragraphs.en: Back outside, Tavi told a passing driver about the blocked road. A taxi could bring people to the warm bath, but no car should continue toward the soft field. The driver agreed to tell others at the next stop. The friends walked home together. They had heard no new song, yet they had learned where not to go. In a long search, that knowledge might be as useful as finding a beautiful place. The child held up his little wooden duck at a window as they left, and Tavi waved back.
paragraphs.zh: 回到戶外，塔薇告訴一位經過的司機道路受阻。計程車可以把人載到暖浴池，但車輛不應繼續前往鬆軟空地。司機答應在下一站提醒其他人。朋友們一起走回家。他們沒有聽到新歌聲，卻知道哪些地方不能去。對長途探索來說，這份知識可能跟找到美景一樣重要。離開時，那孩子在窗邊舉起小木鴨，塔薇也揮手回應。

paragraphs.en: Tavi was still thinking about the old water course when she reached home. She drew the safe path in a strong line and the unknown field in a dotted line. Nell checked the drawing and suggested that they write the word closed next to the field. That word might keep another family from making the same mistake. Ivo wanted to tell everyone about the green ground, but Tavi asked him to explain why it could be soft too. They spoke with the driver before he began his next trip. The driver repeated the warning in his own words so they knew he understood. Tavi felt relieved. The day's best discovery was not a new sound; it was learning that a short path could hide a long risk. Their careful choice gave the next visitors a better chance to travel safely.
paragraphs.zh: 塔薇回家後仍在想舊水道。她用實線畫安全小路，用虛線畫未知空地。奈兒看過後，建議在空地旁寫上「封閉」，可能避免其他家庭犯相同錯誤。伊沃想向大家介紹綠色地面，但塔薇請他同時說明底下為何可能鬆軟。司機出發下一趟前，他們再次說明警告。司機用自己的話重述，讓大家確定他理解了。塔薇鬆了一口氣。這天最好的發現不是新聲音，而是短短的路可能藏著長長的危險。謹慎的決定讓後來的旅人更有機會平安出行。

questions.question: Why was the green field unsafe to cross?
options: Warm water might be under the ground.
questions.explanation: 舊水道可能在綠色空地下方流動，讓地面鬆軟。

questions.question: Who showed them the old water course?
questions.explanation: 奧德太太在地圖上指出舊水道。

title: The Farm on the Moon Road

paragraphs.en: On the next safe day, the friends visited a small farm near a bend called Moon Road. A bank office had helped the farmer buy a new water tank, and he was proud of caring for his animals without waste. He had to feed many hungry mouths before sunrise. A letter from his sister lay on the table, beside a cup of milk. Outside, the moon was still bright. Tavi had come to ask about the birds that once sang in the apple trees. The farmer did not know where they were now, but he offered to walk with them to the end of his land.
paragraphs.zh: 下一個安全的日子，朋友們來到月亮路轉彎處的小農場。銀行曾協助農夫買新水箱，他很自豪能不浪費地照顧動物。日出前，他得餵飽許多張嘴。桌上牛奶旁放著妹妹寄來的信。外頭月亮仍很亮。塔薇是來問以前在蘋果樹上唱歌的鳥。農夫不知道牠們現在在哪裡，但願意陪三人走到農地盡頭。

paragraphs.en: The farmer's daughter, a teenager, showed them an old movie about the farm. In it, a wooden wheel turned beside the well. She said the family did not sell the wheel after buying a pump, because it taught young animals how water moved. The metal parts needed oil, but the wheel was safe to watch from behind the fence when it turned at a slow speed. Today a yellow string kept visitors behind a straight line. Tavi liked the clear rule. The girl asked them to think about the sound of the wheel. Was its low turning sound one of the spring sounds, or was it a sound made by work?
paragraphs.zh: 農夫的十幾歲女兒拿出農場舊影片。影片裡，一個木輪在井邊轉動。她說家人買水泵後沒有賣掉木輪，因為它能教年輕動物了解水怎樣移動。金屬零件需要上油，但當它緩慢轉動時，站在圍欄後觀察是安全的。今天一條黃色繩線讓訪客待在筆直界線後。塔薇喜歡這項清楚規則。女孩請他們想想木輪的聲音：緩慢轉動是春天的聲音，還是工作的聲音？

paragraphs.en: Nell heard a strange tapping from under the empty water tank. She did not step through the fence. Instead, she asked the farmer to check it. He found a loose wooden board and fixed it with a tool. The tapping stopped. Tavi wrote that this sound was not a bird or a stream. She was learning to tell sounds apart without taking risks. Ivo bent down and hurt his toe against a stone, but it was only a small knock. He sat, checked his foot, and rested before walking again.
paragraphs.zh: 奈兒聽見空水箱下傳來奇怪的敲擊聲，沒有跨過圍欄，而是請農夫檢查。農夫發現一塊鬆掉的木板，便用工具固定。敲擊聲停了。塔薇寫下這不是鳥或溪流的聲音。她逐漸學會不冒險也能分辨聲音。伊沃彎腰時腳趾撞上石頭，有點痛，所幸只是輕輕碰傷。他坐下檢查腳，休息後才再走。

paragraphs.en: The family shared bread and sweet apples. Their talk moved from water to the topic of birds. The farmer said that birds often stopped where food was easy to find, but he did not want visitors to bring them meat or other food. Wild animals needed to find their own meals. “Do not decide where they must live,” he said. “Watch where they choose to go.” Tavi agreed. The friends looked through the fence toward the far trees. The branches were empty, but the ground under them was no longer completely white.
paragraphs.zh: 農場一家分享麵包和甜蘋果。他們的談話由水轉到鳥。農夫說鳥常停在容易找到食物的地方，但他不希望訪客帶肉或其他食物去餵。野生動物需要自己找餐食。「不要替牠們決定住哪裡，」他說，「觀察牠們自己去哪裡。」塔薇同意。朋友們隔著圍欄望向遠樹。枝上還沒有鳥，但樹下的地面已不是全白。

paragraphs.en: On the way home, the farmer's daughter walked beside them for a while. She wanted to learn more about listening and asked if she could join on a later day. Tavi said yes, once her family knew the plan. The friends now understood that a quiet place might hold several sounds that seemed alike to a new listener. They needed patience and help from people who knew each place well. As Moon Road disappeared behind the hill, Tavi kept the farm on her map, not as a place to collect birds but as a place to compare what she heard.
paragraphs.zh: 回家路上，農夫的女兒陪他們走了一段。她想多學聆聽，也問以後能否參加。塔薇說可以，但要先讓家人知道計畫。朋友們現在明白，安靜的地方可能藏著幾種對新手聽來很相似的聲音。他們需要耐心，也需要熟悉當地的人協助。月亮路消失在山後時，塔薇仍把農場留在地圖上，不是為了抓鳥，而是方便比較聽見的聲音。

paragraphs.en: The next morning, the farmer's daughter gave them a copy of her notes about the water tank. She had written down how it sounded before the board was fixed and after the work was done. Tavi could now compare two clear examples from the same place. She knew that a change in sound did not always mean a change in season. Sometimes a person had changed a machine. They added a line to their method: ask what changed around the sound. Ivo remembered his sore toe and laughed when he stepped around the same stone on their next visit. The group thanked the family for showing them real work and real care. Tavi also promised not to bring visitors into the farm without asking first. It was a home and a place of work, not an open field for everyone to enter.
paragraphs.zh: 隔天早晨，農夫的女兒交給他們一份水箱紀錄副本。她寫下木板修好前後的聲音。塔薇現在可以比較同一地點的兩個清楚例子。她知道聲音改變不一定是季節改變，有時只是有人修好了機器。他們在方法中增加一項：詢問聲音周圍發生了什麼變化。伊沃想起疼過的腳趾，再次造訪時繞開同一塊石頭，忍不住笑了。團隊感謝這家人展示真實工作和照顧。塔薇也承諾，沒得到允許不會帶訪客進農場。這是住家和工作場所，不是人人可隨意進入的空地。

questions.question: What made a tapping sound at the farm?
questions.explanation: 農夫找到並修好了發出敲聲的鬆木板。

questions.question: Why did Tavi ask before bringing visitors to the farm?
options: It was a private home and workplace.
questions.explanation: 農場是住家與工作場所，訪客不能擅自進入。
